Second moments of the imputed mean and SD from a five-number summary

Source: R/sdf.R
imputed_moments.Rd

Computes \(\mathrm{Var}(\hat\mu)/\sigma^2\), \(\mathrm{Var}(\hat\sigma)/\sigma^2\), \(\mathrm{Cov}(\hat\mu,\hat\sigma)/\sigma^2\) and \(C(n) = \mathrm{SD}(\hat\mu)/\sigma\) for linear estimators \(\hat\mu = w_\mu' Y\), \(\hat\sigma = w_\sigma' Y\) of the reported values \(Y\), under normality, using exact order-statistic moments. The identity used is \(\mathrm{Var}(w'Y) = \sigma^2 w'B_Yw\) (Balakrishnan et al. 2022, eqs. 49-51), where \(B_Y\) is the covariance matrix of the standardized reported values. The default, method_mean = "blue" with method_sd = "blue", is the BLUE, as in every function of the package; method_mean = "luo" with method_sd = NULL gives the estimators of Wan, Luo and Shi.

Usage

imputed_moments(
  n,
  scenario = c("S3", "S1", "S2", "S4", "S5"),
  method_mean = "blue",
  method_sd = "blue",
  w_mean = NULL,
  w_sd = NULL,
  moments = NULL,
  type = 7
)

Arguments

n

Integer sample size: at least 3 under S1 and S2, 5 under S3 and S4, and 7 under S5, under the default quantile definition. Any such n is computed exactly; see Details. Another definition may need a larger \(n\): where two reported values are the same order statistic (type 3 at \(n = 5\) under S3, for example) the BLUE is not defined and is refused.

scenario

Character. One of "S1" (min, median, max), "S2" (three quartiles), "S3" (all five). McGrath 2023 labels; note Wan 2014's C2/C3 are S3/S2 respectively. Also "S4" (the quartiles with the 10th and 90th percentiles) and "S5" (all five with the two percentiles), the names of Wu, Shi and Tong (2026) for Scenarios 5 and 7 of Balakrishnan et al. (2022); only the BLUE ("blue") is defined for these two.

method_mean

Character, NULL or NA. One of "blue" (default), "luo" or "wan", the mean estimator presets of estimator_weights. Ignored if w_mean is given. NULL or NA skips the mean part.

method_sd

Character, NULL or NA. One of "blue" (default), "wan", "shi" (S3 only). NULL pairs Wan's SD under S1 and S2 with Shi's under S3, the pairing of the Wan-Luo-Shi version (Shi 2020 sec. 2 recommends Wan's SD for S1/S2). Ignored if w_sd given. Set to NA to skip the SD part.

w_mean, w_sd

Optional numeric weight vectors overriding the presets (length = number of reported values, in increasing order).

moments

Optional precomputed result of osmoments::os_moments(n, ranks) for the standard normal, at this n and at the ranks that the reported values use (at n = 4Q+1 under type 7 these are scenario_ranks(n, scenario)), or a list with its components alpha and B alone. The sample size, the distribution, the ranks, the location and scale and the shape of alpha and B are checked where the object carries them; a bare list is checked for its size only. The package keeps the moments it computes itself for the session, so repeated calls at one sample size integrate once without this argument.

type

The definition of the sample quantiles, an integer from 1 to 9 as in quantile; 7, R's default, unless a study states another.

Value

A list with components: var_mean \(= w_\mu'Bw_\mu\), var_sd \(= w_\sigma'Bw_\sigma\), cov \(= w_\mu'Bw_\sigma\) (all in units of \(\sigma^2\)); c_n \(= \sqrt{w_\mu'Bw_\mu}\); w_mean, w_sd; gaps: named vector of unbiasedness gaps (mean_sum \(= w_\mu'1 - 1\), mean_alpha \(= w_\mu'\alpha\) = bias of \(\hat\mu\) in \(\sigma\) units, sd_sum \(= w_\sigma'1\), sd_alpha \(= w_\sigma'\alpha - 1\) = relative bias of \(\hat\sigma\)); ranks (the order statistics the reported values use), n, scenario, type.

Details

All second moments are proportional to the true \(\sigma^2\); nothing here plugs in an estimate of \(\sigma\). In particular \(\mathrm{SD}(\hat\mu) = C(n)\sigma\), and the plug-in standard error is \(C(n)\hat\sigma\), not \(\hat\sigma/\sqrt{n}\). Each reported value is an order statistic (the minimum, the maximum) or a sample quantile, which under every definition of quantile is a fixed linear combination \((1-h)X_{(j)} + hX_{(j+1)}\) of two adjacent order statistics (Hyndman and Fan 1996). So \(Y = W'X\), with \(W\) from osmoments::os_quantile_weights(), and the means and covariance matrix of the standardized \(Y\) are \(\alpha_Y = W'\alpha\) and \(B_Y = W'BW\), exact at every \(n\). At \(n = 4Q+1\) under type 7 the quartiles are the order statistics at ranks \(Q+1, 2Q+1, 3Q+1\); at other \(n\), or under another definition, they are interpolated, and the result depends on the definition. Assumptions: i.i.d. normal sample; the reported values follow definition type.

References

Balakrishnan N, Rychtar J, Taylor D, Walter SD (2022). Unified approach to optimal estimation of mean and standard deviation from sample summaries. Statistical Methods in Medical Research 31(11), 2087-2103. (eqs. 49-51) Luo D, Wan X, Liu J, Tong T (2018). Optimally estimating the sample mean from the sample size, median, mid-range, and/or mid-quartile range. Statistical Methods in Medical Research 27(6), 1785-1805. Shi J, Luo D, Weng H, Zeng XT, Lin L, Chu H, Tong T (2020). Optimally estimating the sample standard deviation from the five-number summary. Research Synthesis Methods 11(5), 641-654. Wan X, Wang W, Liu J, Tong T (2014). Estimating the sample mean and standard deviation from the sample size, median, range and/or interquartile range. BMC Medical Research Methodology 14, 135. Yang X, Hutson AD, Wang D (2022). A generalized BLUE approach for combining location and scale information in a meta-analysis. Journal of Applied Statistics 49(15), 3846-3867. (eq. 22) Wu Z, Shi J, Tong T (2026). Precision of the imputed mean and standard deviation from a five-number summary. Manuscript.

Examples

im <- imputed_moments(25, "S3")            # the BLUE of the mean and of the SD, the default
im$c_n                                     # SD(mu-hat)/sigma
#> [1] 0.2068675
imputed_moments(25, "S3", "luo", NULL)$c_n # Luo's mean, with Shi's SD
#> [1] 0.2068703
sqrt(1/25)                                 # naive sigma/sqrt(n) factor, for contrast
#> [1] 0.2
